jobs.jobDescription:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

As Axon’s Senior Supplier Quality Engineer I, you will be responsible for providing Quality Engineering support for all Axon products including Conducted Electrical Weapons (CEW), Cartridges, Body Worn Cameras and accessories. You will be responsible for working with suppliers in cooperation with Axon Design Engineering, Quality and Supply Chain. Other significant impacts will come from collaborating on the selection of qualified suppliers, leading the efforts to quantify and improve supplier performance, and providing a positive impact on the quality of new and existing products through a global footprint.

What You’ll Do

Location: Remote in Vietnam (open for candidates from Hanoi/ Bac Ninh/ Hai Phong/ HCM) at our APAC supplier factories with travel up to 80%

Reports to: Supplier Quality Manager

  • New supplier assessment and supplier audit. Engage in selection and evaluation activities of new potential suppliers and conduct onsite auditing of the supplier to assess quality and/or process related requirements. Audit supplier critical manufacturing & inspection processes, policies and procedures to ensure performance and quality standards conform to established Axon Quality requirements.
  • Ensure New Product Introduction (NPI) takes place in accordance with criteria and inspection plans set up and managed by Axon Program Management, Design and Quality. Reviewing product validation with supplier NPI yield, Jira ticket, OQC, FAIR/PPAP, DFM/DFx, PFMEA and Quality control plan (QCP).
  • Working in close collaboration with our supplier partners, facilitate the development and maintenance of PFMEA to quantify supplier process risks and designing processes to prevent the production of defects. Effect robust assembly operations and manufacturing processes through manufacturability assessment and error-proofing methods to prevent operator errors.
  • Assess supplier inspection capabilities onsite as needed (IQC/OQC/IPQC); Assist in generating appropriate inspection plans and evaluate any inspection and process capability studies provided by suppliers (Cpk, Ppk, Gage R&R).
  • Set up the quality goals and quality improvement projects, monitor the yield rate in suppliers and drive supplier to produce high quality parts consistently with yield improvement month to month.
  • Continuously monitor supplier quality performance and facilitate periodic quality/business reviews to drive continual improvements in DPPM, NCMR’s and SCAR’s. Develop, implement, and monitor supplier quality improvement initiatives, including supplier performance management forums, supplier certification, process improvements, cost reduction, and continuing assessment and process audits of suppliers.
  • Through Quality Control Planning, ensure Critical to Quality (CTQ) product characteristics and key process parameters within the supplier’s manufacturing processes are monitored for process capability and capable of repeatedly producing parts to specifications.

What You Bring

  • Minimum 10 years experiences in problem solving related to manufacturing of mechanical parts (i.e. cast metal parts, molded rubber or plastic parts, cast ceramic parts, machined and stamped parts),
  • Very experienced on the NPI process and milestones, the role of SQE for NPI and the key activities in the NPI stages.
  • Good knowledge of quality management system (QMS) requirements, (ISO9001, ESD20.20, IATF16949, IPC-1602, IPC-A-610 or a comparable certificate and quality criteria), minimum five (5) years' experience in audits utilizing ISO9001, IATF16949, VDA 6.3 or a comparable quality management system.
  • Excellent data analysis, root cause analysis, problem resolution and decision-making skills required with thorough working knowledge of QC tools, methods and practices (PPAP, SPC, DOE, PFMEA, Control Plans, GR&R, Lean Manufacturing concepts, DMAIC, 8D Methodology, etc.)
  • Excellent skills of teamwork and collaboration, able to communicate with all levels of the organization and build relationship with suppliers, ability to influence amongst suppliers and internal groups.
  • Ability to operate in a highly dynamic environment to juggle multiple priorities, to react quickly to emergencies. Excellent time management skills and ability to multi-task and methodically manage project milestones.
  • Excellent written and oral communication in English
  • Experience working with statistical software (i.e. QI Macros, Minitab, JMP)
  • Willing to travel frequently (domestic and international)

Preferred education, certification

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering or Material Engineering
  • Green/black belt, CMQ/OE, CQE and CSSBB certifications preferred

Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Important Notes

The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions.

Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment.

We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at axongreenhousesupport@axon.com or via our Axon Privacy Web Form. For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice.

Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment.

We are an equal opportunity employer that promotes justice, advances equity, values diversity and fosters inclusion. We’re committed to hiring the best talent — regardless of race, creed, color, ancestry, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances — and empowering all of our employees so they can do their best work. If you have a disability or special need that requires assistance or accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email recruitingops@axon.com. Please note that this email address is for accommodation purposes only. Axon will not respond to inquiries for other purposes.

Phishing alert: Axon will never ask you to pay for any part of the hiring process, including training, equipment, or background checks. We do not make job offers via text message, WhatsApp, or instant messaging platforms without a formal interview process. All legitimate job openings are listed on our official careers page at https://www.axon.com/careers. If you receive a suspicious offer or outreach from an email address that is not @axon.com, or if you are asked for sensitive personal information (bank details, Social Security Number) prematurely, please ignore the message and report it to recruitingops@axon.com.

About Binance Accelerator Program

Binance Accelerator Program (BAP) is a 3-6 month internship program designed for Early Career talent to have firsthand experience in the rapidly expanding digital assets space. You will be given the opportunity to develop your skills at Binance and understand what it’s like to work at the world's leading blockchain ecosystem. As part of your internship in the BAP, there will also be opportunities for networking and development, which will expand your professional network and build transferable skills to propel you forward in your career. Learn about the BAP Program HERE.

Who may apply

Current university students and recent graduates.

*Terms of employment / engagement shall be subject to contract and local applicable laws

We are looking for a motivated Product Data Analyst Intern to join our Product DA team. You will work alongside senior analysts on real product analytics projects — including conversion funnel analysis, A/B experiment evaluation, and dashboard building. This is a hands-on role where you'll gain exposure to product strategy, experiment-driven decision making, and large-scale data infrastructure.

Responsibilities:

  • Assist in building and analyzing user conversion funnels, identifying drop-off points and improvement opportunities
  • Support A/B experiment evaluation: pull experiment data, validate cohort allocation (sanity checks), calculate uplift metrics, and summarize results
  • Build and maintain dashboards for key product metrics (CTR, conversion rate, UV/PV)
  • Respond to product team ad-hoc data requests — user segmentation, feature adoption tracking, campaign performance analysis
  • Write and maintain SQL queries for scheduled data pipelines; assist in data quality monitoring
  • Translate data findings into clear summaries and visualizations for product teams

Requirements:

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's/Master's degree in a quantitative discipline (Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Science, or related field)
  • Internship experience in product analytics or related data analysis roles preferred
  • A natural curiosity to identify, investigate and explain trends and patterns in data
  • Bilingual English/Mandarin is required to be able to coordinate with overseas partners and stakeholders.
  • Understanding of A/B testing fundamentals (hypothesis testing, p-value, confidence intervals)
  • Strong logical thinking, attention to detail, and ability to work independently
  • Fast learner with curiosity about product strategy and user behavior
  • Competency in one or more of the following:
  • SQL (able to write complex queries with CTEs, window functions, subqueries)
  • Programming (Python/R for data manipulation)
  • A data visualization tool (e.g. DataWind, Tableau, PowerBI)

Nice to Have

  • Experience with event tracking / behavioral analytics (Sensors, Mixpanel, GA)
  • Familiarity with Airflow or data scheduling tools
  • Interest in crypto/fintech industry
  • Prior experience with large-scale data (Hive/Spark environment)

Compensation

Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

You will expand TRM’s strategic access across the APAC financial institution ecosystem. This is a senior individual contributor role, designed for someone who already has deep credibility and trusted relationships across banks, and financial institutions. You are not being hired to build a network from scratch. You are being hired to activate a network you have already earned. This is not a traditional closing-quota sales role. Your mandate is to open senior-level conversations, multi-thread strategic accounts, create qualified enterprise opportunities, and help TRM become part of the most important digital asset, financial crime, and compliance conversations happening inside major financial institutions.

What You'll Do

  • Open senior-level access at priority APAC financial institutions by activating a network you have already built.

  • Build multi-threaded relationships across the stakeholders who shape digital asset strategy, financial crime programs, compliance priorities, investigations, risk, and innovation.

  • Help TRM earn a seat in the most important conversations happening inside strategic financial institutions Identify and pursue high-value enterprise and partnership opportunities with banks and other financial institutions.

  • Represent TRM externally at conferences, executive forums, practitioner communities, and industry events, turning public presence and private conversations into qualified opportunities.

  • Partner closely with Sales, Product, Marketing, and Policy to turn strategic access into qualified customer opportunities, market insight, and long-term competitive advantage.

  • Close the loop between field signal and internal strategy by feeding customer insights, buying dynamics, objections, and market intelligence back into TRM’s product and GTM teams.

What We're Looking For

  • Deep, credible network across APAC financial institutions, ideally from having been head of digital assets at a bank, or from operating at a crypto infrastructure firm

  • Comfortable being customer-facing and public-facing: conferences, panels, thought leadership

  • Track record of turning relationships into real pipeline, not just introductions

  • Already uses AI day-to-day for research, prospecting, and pipeline management, with a concrete workflow to point to

Hard Requirements

  • Based in Singapore, remote

  • Willing to travel 30-40% for conferences and in-person account work

  • Direct experience with financial institutions or crypto-native infrastructure companies serving them in APAC

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure you’re considered.

What to Expect From Our Interview Process

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while giving you the opportunity to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, AI skills assessment, and Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Explore your experience, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Dive deeper into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: Typically 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Meet some of the people you'd be working with. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper on your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: We’ll speak with former colleagues who can provide perspective on your work and impact.

  • Offer: If it’s a mutual fit, your recruiter will walk you through your offer and answer your questions.

  • Welcome to TRM: Once you sign, we’ll get you ready for your first day and onboarding.

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

Learn more about interviewing at TRM

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves quickly. We are a high velocity, high ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly as we experiment and iterate

  • Work that often requires operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires comfort navigating ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

At the same time, many people find this work deeply rewarding. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. Learn more about Interviewing at TRM

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.   • Work the intelligence flywheel operationally — processing investigative returns at high volume and feeding victim, operator, and infrastructure data into TRM’s intelligence and product pipelines.

  • Find the seams — pivot from a single victim, wallet, device, or compound lead into uncovering broader operational networks and multiplying investigative leads.

  • Partner with TRM’s Scams SME team, on-chain analysts, and the DC-based targeting cell to translate regional collection and disruption strategy into targeting packages that support government enforcement actions.

What we're looking for:

  • US Citizenship required. Bangkok presence or extensive APAC travel required.

  • 5-8+ years of all-source investigative or targeting experience — federal law enforcement (former 1811s — e.g., FBI, HSI, IRS-CI, Secret Service), Intelligence Community all-source analysis, or mission-aligned private sector equivalent

  • Operational Leadership — Proven experience building targeting packages for intelligence or law enforcement partners and coordinating small analytic teams or investigative pods in a player-coach capacity.

  • OSINT Tradecraft — Hands-on experience with cell triangulation, IP geolocation, GEOINT, AdTech analysis, and infrastructure attribution.

  • Targeting & Analysis Skills — Proven ability to build operational intelligence products and pivot from a single lead into broader operational networks using strong link and pattern analysis.

  • APAC Operational Experience — Southeast Asia field experience (particularly Thailand, Myanmar, Laos, or Cambodia) strongly preferred; regional language skills are a major differentiator.

  • AI & Investigative Fluency — Comfortable using AI tools to accelerate investigative workflows, synthesize data, and draft operational outputs.

  • Mission Alignment — Financial crime or crypto experience is a plus, not a requirement.

  • Close collaboration with TRM's Scams SME team, who provide foundational scam compound domain context

  • Daily async standups via Slack on active work, returns, and target packages in flight

  • Primary time zone overlap: US Eastern / APAC

jobs.jobDescription:
About the team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. OpenAI for Government (OAI4G) helps public-sector institutions understand, adopt, and deploy highly capable AI products in support of their missions. The team brings together Sales, Solutions, Partnerships, Technical Success, Legal, Security, Policy, Global Affairs, and other cross-functional partners to help governments use AI responsibly and effectively.

As part of OAI4G’s International Public Sector team, you will help public institutions in Australia and New Zealand (ANZ) and APAC translate frontier AI into secure, compliant, mission-aligned outcomes. We work across varied procurement, regulatory, security, sovereignty, and commercial environments, while maintaining a consistent commitment to safety, reliability, and public benefit.

About the role

We are seeking a senior Account Director (AD) to lead OpenAI’s public-sector work across ANZ, with a wider remit to develop selected priority opportunities across APAC. ANZ will be the centre of gravity for the role: you will build trusted relationships with government leaders, develop and execute account strategies, create and close complex opportunities, and help customers move from initial interest to successful adoption.

This is a full-cycle, highly cross-functional sales role that combines technical understanding, strategic vision, partnership management, and value-driven execution. You will work with senior government, operational, technical, procurement, policy, and security stakeholders to identify high-impact AI use cases and translate them into credible commercial and deployment pathways across the OpenAI Platform API and Codex and ChatGPT Enterprise.

You will also be an accountable customer leader after signature, working alongside specialist delivery and technical teams to keep customer outcomes, milestones, adoption, risks, and executive alignment on track. The role requires excellent judgement, executive presence, local fluency, and the ability to move between strategy, discovery, capture, procurement, delivery governance, and relationship management without day-to-day direction.

This role can be based in Sydney (Hybrid model, 3 days in office) or remotely from Canberra.

In this role, you will

  • Own a focused portfolio of ANZ public-sector accounts, while developing selected priority opportunities in APAC in line with OAI4G’s international strategy.

  • Build and execute comprehensive account plans that map mission priorities, stakeholders, procurement paths, partners, use cases, risks, and long-term expansion opportunities.

  • Drive complex opportunities through the full sales cycle, from pipeline generation, discovery, qualification, capture, and commercial strategy through negotiation, closure, adoption, and expansion.

  • Lead public-sector customers through their AI adoption journey, helping them identify responsible, high-impact use cases and connect mission outcomes to OpenAI’s capabilities and limitations.

  • Translate between government leaders, end users, technical teams, policy and security stakeholders, and internal product and engineering partners, clearly communicating requirements, progress, risks, and dependencies.

  • Serve as the accountable customer lead for engagements tied to clear outcomes, customer milestones, adoption measures, and commercial commitments, coordinating closely with technical specialists.

  • Work closely with the Partnerships team, global and regional system integrators, cloud and technology providers, local delivery partners, resellers, and strategic international partners to shape joint pursuits, deployment models, and purchasing paths.

  • Develop capture strategies, competitive positioning, win themes, teaming decisions, and proposal narratives that reflect ANZ and relevant APAC market conditions.

  • Navigate public-sector procurement, tendering, security, data-residency, compliance, and sovereignty requirements, bringing Legal, Security, Policy, Global Affairs, Finance, and other partners into opportunities early.

  • Build trusted relationships with senior government executives and decision-makers, while staying close to operational users and technical stakeholders whose workflows determine successful adoption.

  • Maintain accurate pipeline, forecasting, account records, customer follow-up, and executive reporting, with disciplined follow-through across markets and time zones.

  • Monitor the government, technology, procurement, partner, and competitive landscape across ANZ and priority APAC markets, surfacing insights that inform product roadmaps and go-to-market strategy.

  • Represent OpenAI at government, partner, and industry forums, strengthening networks and identifying opportunities that advance responsible public-sector adoption of AI.

We’re seeking someone with experience including

  • 10+ years in government, public-sector technology sales, business development, consulting, transformation, systems integration, or a closely related field, with meaningful ownership of complex customer outcomes.

  • Direct government experience or very significant experience working with government customers, ideally including sensitive agencies, national-security-adjacent environments, regulated missions, or high-consequence operational workflows.

  • A current Australian Government security clearance, with the ability to maintain the clearance required for the role.

  • Designing and executing complex deal strategies, including opportunity shaping before formal procurement, multi-stakeholder qualification, proposal development, negotiations, and closure.

  • Working directly with senior public-sector executives and decision-makers, alongside technical, operational, procurement, policy, and security stakeholders.

  • Navigating Australia’s public-sector procurement, contracting, security, privacy, data-residency, and compliance requirements; familiarity with New Zealand and/or other APAC public-sector environments is valuable.

  • Selling or delivering enterprise SaaS, cloud, AI/ML, data platforms, cybersecurity, API-based products, or other complex technology solutions in highly regulated environments.

  • Communicating technical, commercial, and strategic concepts clearly to both executive and working-level audiences, including the ability to explain where AI is and is not an appropriate fit.

  • Collaborating across Sales, Solutions, Partnerships, Research, Engineering, Technical Success, Legal, Security, Policy, Global Affairs, Finance, and Operations to move complex opportunities forward.

  • Operating with high ownership and sound judgement in ambiguous, fast-changing environments, while managing competing priorities across countries and time zones.

  • Travelling regularly within ANZ, and periodically across APAC, to work on-site with customers and partners.

Nice to have

  • Deep relationships across Australian Commonwealth, state and territory, defence, national security, or other sensitive public-sector communities.

  • Experience building or working through local system-integrator, reseller, cloud-provider, or strategic-partner ecosystems.

  • Experience leading AI, digital, technology, or business-transformation initiatives from use-case shaping through deployment and adoption.

  • Familiarity with public-sector AI governance, responsible AI, cybersecurity, data sovereignty, and assurance requirements.

  • Experience developing opportunities across more than one APAC market and adapting to different political, cultural, regulatory, and procurement contexts.

  • Engineering, technical, policy, or operational experience that helps you translate complex AI capabilities into credible public-sector outcomes.

You will thrive in this role if you

  • Are customer-centric. You work to understand public institutions’ missions and constraints deeply, and help them achieve meaningful outcomes with AI.

  • Are a strategist. You think years ahead, balance ANZ priorities with a broader APAC perspective, and align internal and external stakeholders around a clear point of view.

  • Are a builder. You create repeatable account, partner, capture, and delivery practices that can scale while adapting to local requirements.

  • Have strong judgement. You can navigate sensitive environments, incomplete information, competing priorities, and responsible-use considerations with integrity and composure.

  • Are technically curious. You can learn quickly, engage credibly with specialists, and translate frontier AI capabilities, limitations, and trade-offs for government audiences.

  • Care about public mission impact. You want to help governments use AI responsibly and effectively in ways that improve outcomes for the communities they serve.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link.

OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy

At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology.

jobs.jobDescription:
Not all heroes wear capes — but plenty of them use toilet paper

Want to challenge yourself at a purpose-led scale up AND make a difference in the world? Come join the revolootion!

Funny name, serious business

We are a leading eco-friendly household essentials business and we donate 50% of our profits to help everyone gain access to clean water and a toilet. As of June 2024, we’ve contributed over $20 million AUD to this mission. Basically, we’re really good at making it easy to do good.

We operate scaling businesses the UK, US, Australia and Canada. Our amazing team is based in Australia, the UK, the Philippines, China, and the US. Our 250+ people aim to make the biggest possible impact for people and the planet. Over the next 5-10 years, we’re hoping to increase our annual donation tenfold to get us closer to our dream of everyone in the world having access to clean water and sanitation services.

A bit about the role

As our AR & AP Lead, you’ll be the eyes and ears of our Number Scrunchers accounting function — driving accounts receivable and accounts payable operations day to day, in close partnership with your two direct reports (our AR Expert and AP Coordinator) and the wider Financial Operations team. You’ll keep our books accurate, our customers paying on time, and our suppliers paid on time, all so we can maximise the donations we’re able to make.

If you worked here this past month here are some things you might have been involved in

  • Pulled together the monthly AR ageing report for the CFO and exec team, with a clear plan to chase down aged amounts
  • Reviewed the weekly payments file (including the Tipalti funding summary) before it went out for approval
  • Flagged an “at risk” customer account early and looped in the customer-facing team for support
  • Helped close the books accurately and on time at month-end, escalating one risk early to the Head of Financial Operations
  • Worked with the AP Coordinator to tidy up a clunky step in the AP process

Let’s talk about you

Detail is your love language

You get real satisfaction from a reconciliation that ties out perfectly and a report that lands on the CFO’s desk without a single follow-up question. You’re equally comfortable rolling your sleeves up in the detail of a customer account and stepping back to build the KPIs and reporting that keep the whole team honest.

Calm under a closing calendar

Month-end doesn’t rattle you. You know how to keep AR and AP on track to a deadline, spot a risk early enough to actually do something about it, and communicate clearly with stakeholders when something needs to change.

A coach as much as a doer

You lead a small, tight-knit team and genuinely enjoy it — you give clear, kind feedback, help your people grow, and aren’t afraid of a difficult conversation when a process or a stakeholder relationship needs a repair job.

You give a crap. Do you want your work to make the world a better place? Do you want to work with other people who feel the same way? What a coincidence — us too!

Why should you work with us?

First off, as a certified B Corp™, we work to make a difference every day while maintaining the high standards of social and environmental impact. We’re in very good company with other exceptional B Corps around the world.

We also believe that helping to make the world a better place should be rewarded accordingly – that’s why we offer competitive, market informed salaries, meaningful support towards healthcare for our team around the world, generous paid leave, tailored learning and development opportunities, and free toilet paper (yes, you read that right).

Our engagement surveys (thanks Culture Amp!) tell us that our team is really proud (over 90%) to work for Who Gives A Crap and, well, we couldn’t be more proud of that.

Have you made it this far?

If you’re still reading, we think there’s a strong chance you might be our kind of person. Here’s the thing, though — research suggests that 60% of women and underrepresented folks might have already talked themselves out of applying. Even if you don’t check every box above, we want to encourage you to introduce yourself. We believe a diversity of perspectives and experiences makes a team stronger — and the stronger our team, the closer we are to delivering toilets and clean water for all.

At Instructure, we believe in the power of people to grow and succeed throughout their lives. Our goal is to amplify that power by creating intuitive products that simplify learning and personal development, facilitate meaningful relationships, and inspire people to go further in their education and careers.
We do this by giving smart, creative, passionate people opportunities to create awesome. And that's where you come in:

Customer Success Managers are part of Instructure’s Customer Success team and act as trusted partners to our customers.

In this role, you’ll own the customer relationship across a portfolio of education customers in Asia, helping them realise measurable value from the Instructure ecosystem, achieve their strategic goals, and build a strong foundation for long-term success. You’ll take a consultative, proactive approach: understanding each customer’s priorities, bringing structure to their success journey, identifying risk early, supporting renewal readiness, and recognising opportunities for growth. Success in this role is measured through customer outcomes, value realisation, strong relationships, retention, and growth.

As a CSM you will be:

  • Partnering with customers across Asia in the Education sector, acting as a trusted advisor and taking ownership of the overall customer relationship and outcomes.

  • Building strategic, multi-threaded relationships across customer organisations, including champions, decision-makers and executive stakeholders.

  • Developing a deep understanding of each customer’s strategic priorities, business drivers and challenges, and translating these into clear success plans, measurable outcomes and value.

  • Driving adoption and value realisation across the Instructure ecosystem, helping customers use our products and services to achieve their institutional goals.

  • Owning customer renewal readiness and confidence, proactively identifying risk, changes in sentiment and barriers to long-term success well ahead of renewal.

  • Identifying, qualifying and progressing growth opportunities aligned to customer priorities, partnering closely with Sales and Renewals to support expansion.

  • Leading purposeful customer engagements including strategic planning, value reviews and executive conversations, with clear outcomes and next steps.

  • Coordinating effectively across Support, Services, Product, Sales and other internal teams to resolve customer challenges and progress customer outcomes.

  • Advocating for customers by providing meaningful insight and feedback to Product and Engineering that helps improve the customer experience and our solutions.

  • Maintaining clear visibility of customer strategy, risk, opportunities, actions and next steps through disciplined use of our Customer Success systems and processes.

  • Contributing to cross-functional initiatives that improve the way Customer Success operates across APAC.

Ideally, you will have:

  • Strong empathy and curiosity, with the ability to understand customer needs and communicate complex topics in an authentic, practical and relatable way.

  • A strong sense of ownership and accountability, with the ability to identify what needs to happen, form a clear recommendation and drive actions through to an outcome.

  • Commercial awareness and confidence discussing customer value, renewal risk and growth opportunities.

  • Experience building trusted relationships across multiple stakeholder levels, including senior and executive stakeholders.

  • Strong strategic thinking combined with the operational discipline required to manage a portfolio of customers effectively.

  • Sound judgement and prioritisation skills, with the ability to focus effort where it will have the greatest customer and commercial impact.

  • Clear and concise written and verbal English communication skills, with the ability to adapt your communication style to different audiences.

  • Enthusiasm for education and technology, with demonstrated technical aptitude and an ability to learn new products and concepts quickly.

  • Experience using CRM, Customer Success or project management tools to manage customer activity, workflows and portfolio visibility.

  • A results-driven mindset and a willingness to learn, collaborate and operate effectively in a dynamic environment.

  • Experience in education or Educational Technology would be highly regarded.

  • At least 2-4 years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management or a related customer-facing SaaS role, ideally within Educational Technology.

  • Fluency in English is required. Fluency in one or more additional APAC languages, such as Tagalog, Cantonese, Mandarin, Malay, Japanese or Bahasa Indonesia, is desirable but not essential.

jobs.jobDescription:
About Zscaler

Zscaler accelerates digital transformation to ensure our customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. As an AI-forward enterprise, we are constantly pushing the envelope, leveraging the world’s largest security data lake to power our cloud-native Zero Trust Exchange platform. This innovation protects our customers from cyberattacks and data loss by securely connecting users, devices, and applications in any location.

Here, impact in your role matters more than title and trust is built on results. We say, impact over activity. We seek innovators who actively use AI to amplify their impact and who thrive in an environment where we leverage intelligent systems to stay ahead of evolving threats. We believe in transparency and value constructive, honest debate—we’re focused on getting to the best ideas, faster. We build high-performing teams that can make an impact quickly and with high quality. To do this, we are building a culture of execution centered on customer obsession, collaboration, ownership, and accountability.

We value high-impact, high-accountability with a sense of urgency where you’re enabled to do your best work and embrace your potential. If you’re driven by purpose, thrive on solving complex challenges, and want to be part of the team that’s helping to secure the AI age, we invite you to bring your talents to Zscaler and help shape the future of cybersecurity.

The Team

The Zscaler Sales and Go-to-Market team is a global group of professionals who are passionate about delighting our customers, nurturing trusted partnerships, and sharing their expertise to guide a secure, cloud-enabled digital future and further cement our position as the world leader in cloud security. Sales, Customer Success, Sales Enablement, Solution Architects, Business Development, Transformation, and Technology Partnerships all work together to demonstrate the power and agility of Zscaler cloud transformation to the world.

The Role

We are looking for a dynamic and enthusiastic Senior Account Executive (AE) - AI Security to join our Japan based team based in Tokyo to help accelerate growth in the highly competitive world of AI cybersecurity. This is both a customer acquisition and customer management role that combines communication skills, a consultative approach, and business / sales expertise to demonstrate the value of our platform from discovery calls closing projects.

As a Sr. AE, you will speak with dozens of new people every week including CISOs, AI development engineers, and security leaders. You will strive to form lasting customer relationships with the goal of building champions of Zscaler for years to come. You’ll also channel customer insights back into Zscaler’s product roadmap and marketing, helping us continuously push the frontier of AI security.

What You’ll Do

  • Strategic prospecting and driving GTM motion: Research and prospect into organizations using email, calls, networking, and other creative methods to guide early-stage pipeline development.
  • Lead qualification: Penetrate, profile, qualify, and schedule well-qualified appointments with key decision-makers within targeted companies.
  • Activity Goals: You will exceed daily and weekly activity goals, delivering a high quantity of well-qualified sales opportunities.
  • Articulating our value proposition in AI Security: To assess buying interest, you will articulate our value proposition to decision makers across multiple industries.
  • Technical Understanding: You will attain a deep understanding and demonstrate Zscaler tech solutions to prospective clients about AI Security.
  • Work closely with Sales Engineers in the sales process with potential prospects and customers.
  • Research and Education: You will research customers, identify decision-makers, educate prospects, and qualify buying interest.
  • Develop business value propositions based on customer situations and Zscaler offerings.
  • Communicate customer needs and objections to product and marketing teams.
  • Represent Zscaler at conferences and trade shows including booth work and networking sessions.
  • Maintain awareness of competitors and their products that compete against Zscaler products.

Who You Are (Minimum Qualifications)

  • Foundational understanding of AI/ML technologies and experience leveraging, securing, or positioning AI-driven solutions to optimize outcomes within your functional domain
  • Experienced in customer-facing GTM roles, ideally within cybersecurity or GenAI environments.
  • Knowledgeable in Generative AI, cybersecurity, or adjacent technical domains.
  • Skilled communicator, equally comfortable in c level meetings and executive briefings.
  • Strong problem-solver with a track record of resolving AI and business-related problems.
  • Experience with the MEDDIC sales methodology.
  • 5+ years of full sales cycle experience within software or security industry.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent education.

Why Join Zscaler?

  • Be part of the defining security challenge of our era: enabling safe AI adoption at enterprise scale.
  • Help shape the AI security category at a pivotal moment of growth.
  • Work with world-class red teamers, engineers, and security leaders.
  • Remote-first flexibility, with opportunities for travel and event representation.
  • Direct impact: your work directly shapes outcomes for Fortune 500 enterprises and beyond.

At Zscaler, we are committed to building a team that reflects the communities we serve and the customers we work with. We foster an inclusive environment that values all backgrounds and perspectives, emphasizing collaboration and belonging. Join us in our mission to make doing business seamless and secure.

Our Benefits program is one of the most important ways we support our employees. Zscaler proudly offers comprehensive and inclusive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families throughout their life stages, including:

  • Various health plans
  • Time off plans for vacation and sick time
  • Parental leave options
  • Retirement options
  • Education reimbursement
  • In-office perks, and more!

Learn more about Zscaler's hybrid working model and benefits here.

By applying for this role, you adhere to applicable laws, regulations, and Zscaler policies, including those related to security and privacy standards and guidelines.

Zscaler is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all individuals. We strive to create a workplace where employees are treated with respect and have the chance to succeed. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy or related medical conditions), age, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. See more information by clicking on the Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal link.

Pay Transparency

Zscaler complies with all applicable federal, state, and local pay transparency rules.

Zscaler is committed to providing reasonable support (called accommodations or adjustments) in our recruiting processes for candidates who are differently abled, have long term conditions, mental health conditions or sincerely held religious beliefs, or who are neurodivergent or require pregnancy-related support.

At Instructure, we believe in the power of people to grow and succeed throughout their lives. Our goal is to amplify that power by creating intuitive products that simplify learning and personal development, facilitate meaningful relationships, and inspire people to go further in their education and careers.
We do this by giving smart, creative, passionate people opportunities to create awesome. And that's where you come in:

Foundry is a standalone division inside Instructure, built to generate new revenue with AI-built products. You’re the growth engine for the pods. In the core business, this work splits across product marketing, demand generation, content, and lifecycle teams; here, it’s one person doing all of it — finding the message that lands, filling the early-access pipeline, and turning a working product into paying customers. You’ll set positioning, generate demand, and own the funnel from first touch to renewal, working hand in hand with Pod Founders who are selling as they build. This is a blank-page job: most pods start with no category, no audience list, and no playbook, and you’ll build all three. The role reports to the President, Foundry, with a matrixed dotted line to Instructure’s Marketing leadership.

What you’ll do:

  • Own positioning and messaging. Craft the value proposition, naming, and packaging input for products customers have never heard of, and maintain messaging frameworks by segment across K12, higher education, and business and government.

  • Run go-to-market and launch. Own go-to-market readiness for pilots, early access, and general availability — timelines, channels, pricing input, and the launch assets that carry the story.

  • Build the demand engine. Generate pipeline through campaigns, audience building, early-access recruiting, and the top of the funnel that feeds the Founder’s selling.

  • Drive content. Create the collateral, digital content, and customer-facing assets that build demand and make the differentiation obvious.

  • Be the market and customer expert. Become the go-to expert on the portfolio’s customers and competitors, and feed that insight back into product and pricing.

  • Own lifecycle and adoption. Once customers land, drive adoption, expansion, and retention with consistent, value-based messaging.

  • Measure and adjust. Track funnel and campaign performance against pipeline and revenue, and change course fast when the numbers say so.

What you’ll need:

  • Five or more years in product, portfolio, or growth marketing, ideally in ed tech or a related industry, with new-product launches under your belt.

  • A demonstrated ability to drive go-to-market strategy and execute strategic product launches end to end.

  • Demand-generation range — campaigns, funnel, and audience building — not just positioning and decks.

  • Strong writing, with a portfolio of strategically focused content and collateral.

  • The ability to influence executive and cross-functional teams, and to present to groups large and small, virtually and in person.

  • A full-stack marketer’s range — you do product marketing, demand generation, content, and lifecycle yourself, and you market to fill pipeline and close revenue, not to win awards.

This role isn’t for everyone:

You should probably pass if:

  • You want to own one slice — just messaging, or just campaigns — and hand off the rest.

  • You need an established brand and a built-in audience to market into. Here you build the category.

  • You measure success by impressions and activity rather than by pipeline and revenue.

  • You want a large marketing organization with clear lanes. This is one person, broad scope, and fast.

jobs.jobDescription:
About Halter.

At Halter, we're on a mission to enable farmers and producers to run the most productive and sustainable operations in the world. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the constraints of conventional practices, and revolutionising pasture farming with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry.

People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you'll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care.

The Role.

We're looking for an exceptional Sales Engineer to join Halter's Enterprise Sales team, partnering with the largest and most influential farming businesses across New Zealand and Australia.

This is not a traditional pre-sales engineering role. You'll become a trusted technical advisor to some of agriculture's most progressive organisations. You'll combine commercial awareness and technical expertise to solve complex operational challenges. Whether you're designing enterprise roll-out strategies, validating technical solutions, or influencing the future direction of our product, you'll play a critical role in helping our largest customers succeed.

You'll work alongside Enterprise Sales Managers and Key Account Managers throughout complex sales cycles, providing technical leadership from first engagement through to implementation planning.

You'll also become the voice of enterprise customers within Halter, ensuring the product continues to evolve to meet the needs of the world's leading farming businesses.

What your day could look like.

Enterprise Discovery & Solution Design

You'll work with Enterprise Sales Managers to deeply understand a customer's farming system, operational model and strategic priorities. You'll identify where Halter creates value, design technical solutions that meet complex enterprise requirements, and help customers envision what operating differently could look like across dozens of farms.

Technical Leadership

You'll become the technical expert in enterprise engagements, leading product demonstrations, solution workshops, technical discovery sessions and implementation planning. You'll confidently answer detailed questions around grazing systems, hardware, connectivity, integrations, data, reporting and large-scale deployments.

Customer Problem Solving

No two enterprise customers operate the same way. You'll enjoy unpacking complex operational challenges and collaborating with customers to develop practical solutions. You'll work with multiple stakeholders, from farm managers and operational leaders through to executives and boards, ensuring Halter can be successfully adopted across their organisation.

Product & Customer Feedback

You'll be the bridge between enterprise customers and Halter's Product and Engineering teams. You'll identify emerging customer needs, recurring product opportunities and market trends, helping shape the evolution of Halter as we continue to scale globally.

Cross-functional Execution

Enterprise customers require seamless execution. You'll work closely with Sales, Account Management, Customer Success, and Halter's world class Product and Engineering team to ensure technical alignment throughout the customer journey and support successful roll-outs across large farming portfolios.

Build What's Next

As Halter scales, you'll help establish best practice for enterprise solution engineering. You'll contribute to technical playbooks, customer tools, implementation frameworks and internal capability that allows Halter to serve increasingly complex customers around the world.

Who are we looking for?

We're looking for someone who thrives on solving difficult problems and who is excited at the prospect of sitting at the intersection of agriculture, bleeding edge technology and commercial strategy.

You'll likely bring:

  • Experience in technical pre-sales, solution engineering, implementation consulting or a similar customer-facing technical role.

  • It's not a deal breaker, but an understanding of commercial farming systems, ideally dairy or livestock production.

  • The ability to simplify complex technical concepts for both operational and executive audiences.

  • Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with confidence facilitating workshops and influencing senior stakeholders.

  • Curiosity and systems thinking. You naturally enjoy understanding how complex businesses operate and identifying better ways of working.

  • High ownership and accountability. You enjoy ambiguity, move quickly and take responsibility for outcomes.

  • A collaborative mindset and a passion for working across Product, Engineering and Commercial teams.

  • A desire to build. As Halter grows, you'll help define how enterprise solution engineering operates for years to come.

  • Good vibes and fun to the Enterprise team and our customers.

Frequent travel is part of this role, you'll engage with customers across New Zealand and Australia regularly.

If building the future of farming excites you, we'd love to hear from you.

Join our team

Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement. If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!

Please also feel free to check out the careers page for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn & Instagram.

Why our team loves working at Halter:

  • Work that genuinely matters. Every now and again a company comes along that transforms an entire industry and leaves the world in a better place. Our team gets to be part of something truly meaningful, helping farmers improve their livelihoods, spend more time with their families, and build more sustainable operations.

  • Spectacular people solving hard problems. Our culture is designed for talented people to do work that changes lives. The team is filled with diverse, kind, and driven people who push each other to do their best work. You'll be thrown into the deep end, tackling complex challenges and building something tangible that solves real problems.

  • You'll grow here. Autonomy, mastery, and learning define how we work. You'll have the freedom to work on interesting problems, master new skills, and continuously develop yourself, both through your role and our $1,000 personal growth fund.

  • This isn't easy, and we love that it's hard. Working at Halter will be the most rewarding and the most challenging work of your life. We move fast, take bold bets, and work hard to reshape an entire industry. As one team member put it: "Joining Halter is a bit like strapping yourself to a rocket ship, but it's an epic journey to be a part of!"

jobs.jobDescription:
About Halter

At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.

We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund, Bessemer Venture Partners, BOND, DCVC, Blackbird, Promus Ventures, Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram.

About the role

Halter's component suppliers are predominantly based across Asia. The components they produce have to be right before they ever reach our contract manufacturers. When something is wrong, we need someone on the ground who can get to the root cause fast, push through to a real fix, and prevent it from happening again.

The Supplier Quality Principal is Halter's senior technical authority embedded in Asia. You'll lead highly technical supplier audits, own complex quality problem-solving at our suppliers, and work directly with both suppliers and Halter's design teams to ensure that what comes off a supplier's production line meets the standard we set. You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy, covering a portfolio of suppliers across the region and acting as the technical bridge between our Asia supply base and the Halter team in Auckland.

This is not a compliance role. Ticking audit checkboxes and filing reports is not what this job is about. The best person for this role is someone who goes deep: who can walk a production line and immediately identify what's controlling quality and what isn't, who can sit with a supplier's engineers and work through a failure mode from first principles, and who knows the difference between a corrective action that actually solves a problem and one that just looks good on paper.

You'll report to the Head of Supplier Quality and work closely with Halter's hardware design and operations teams. When there's a quality issue in Asia that needs solving, you're the person we call.

You'll be measured on the technical quality of audits, the speed and effectiveness of issue resolution at suppliers, and your ability to build supplier capability over time.

What You'll Do

Technical Supplier Auditing

  • Lead technically rigorous audits of Halter's component suppliers across Asia, going well beyond system compliance to assess process control, measurement capability, and the reliability of how suppliers actually build and inspect parts.

  • Identify the real drivers of quality performance at a supplier, not just the documented procedures, and develop clear, prioritised findings that distinguish between critical risks and cosmetic gaps.

  • Conduct pre-qualification audits of new suppliers, assessing their technical capability and readiness to meet Halter's design and quality requirements before commitments are made.

  • Run periodic surveillance audits to verify that corrective actions have been implemented effectively and that quality performance is being sustained.

  • Develop and continuously improve Halter's audit methodology and supplier assessment criteria, ensuring audits capture what actually matters for component quality.

Technical Problem Solving

  • Own the resolution of complex quality issues at suppliers, using first-principles analysis to identify root cause and drive effective corrective actions rather than superficial fixes.

  • When a production failure or OQC rejection occurs, lead rapid on-site analysis with supplier engineers and Halter's design team to understand the failure mode, assess risk to in-flight inventory, and define the fastest path to resolution.

  • Work with suppliers to improve their process controls, measurement systems, and inspection methods so that quality issues are caught and corrected at source, not downstream.

  • Coach supplier engineering teams to develop their own capability for root cause analysis and corrective action, building their ability to self-solve rather than depend on Halter for every issue.

  • Escalate issues clearly and early when resolution is taking too long, a supplier is not engaging in good faith, or a quality risk to production is emerging.

Quality Assurance Specifications

  • Implement and maintain Halter's quality assurance specifications at suppliers, ensuring specifications are understood, accepted, and consistently applied across the production process.

  • Work with Halter's hardware design team and the Head of Supplier Quality to refine QA specifications where field experience, audit findings, or supplier feedback reveals gaps or ambiguity.

  • Ensure that when designs evolve, updated specifications are communicated to suppliers, implemented correctly, and re-validated before affected parts re-enter supply.

  • Challenge specifications that are unclear, unmeasurable, or misaligned with what suppliers can realistically control, bringing engineering and operations teams to a better standard.

Part Approval and Ongoing Compliance

  • Support supplier-side part approval activities, ensuring new and revised components are formally validated against Halter's specifications before production release.

  • Maintain a clear picture of approval status and open quality issues across the suppliers in your portfolio, tracking corrective actions to closure and flagging risks to supply continuity.

  • Collaborate with the Head of Contract Manufacturing Quality when parts that pass supplier OQC fail IQC at our contract manufacturers, working to determine whether root cause sits with the supplier process, the OQC criteria, or the incoming inspection.

Supplier Development

  • Build genuine working relationships with quality and engineering counterparts at key suppliers, creating the trust and technical credibility that allows hard conversations to happen fast.

  • Identify where suppliers have systemic capability gaps and develop structured improvement plans that address root cause, not symptoms.

  • Share Halter's standards, expectations, and technical knowledge with suppliers in a way that builds their capability over time rather than creating dependency.

What You Bring

  • 15 or more years of experience in supplier quality or manufacturing quality for complex electromechanical hardware, with a proven track record of solving technically difficult quality problems at suppliers.

  • Deep manufacturing and process engineering knowledge. You understand how parts are made, what drives process variation, and how to identify whether a supplier's process is actually in control.

  • Exceptional audit capability. You conduct audits that go beneath the surface, uncover the real quality risks, and produce findings that drive meaningful improvement.

  • Strong first-principles thinking. When you see a quality failure, you work back to the actual root cause, not the nearest plausible explanation.

  • Experience with QA specification development and the ability to assess whether a specification is clear, measurable, and correctly implemented at a supplier.

  • High proficiency in both English and Mandarin (written, verbal, and reading). You can work directly with Chinese engineers and leadership without translation.

  • Comfortable operating autonomously across a portfolio of suppliers. You manage your own priorities, escalate the right things at the right time, and don't need close supervision to stay effective.

  • Firm, fair, and direct with suppliers. You hold a high standard, push back on inadequate corrective actions, and maintain a relationship that is professional and productive even when conversations are hard.

  • Willing to travel regularly across APAC. A significant portion of your time will be on-site at suppliers.

  • A Master's degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline is preferred.

Join our team

Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.

We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund, Bessemer Venture Partners, BOND, DCVC, Blackbird, Promus Ventures, Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram.

About the roleHalter is searching for a Lead Supply Quality Engineer to take responsibility for ensuring that every component in our supply chain is delivered at quality and on time.

If you are an expert in implementing and managing quality systems to catch issues early, resolve them quickly, and ensure high-quality components are always delivered on-time at our Contract Manufacturers, we want to talk to you!

Our Hardware manufacturing is accelerating quickly to satisfy our growing global markets and it is vital that every component that is shipped to our contract manufacturers in Asia is ready for the tough environment it will face on farm, once it is assembled into Halter hardware.

What your day could look like

  • Implement statistical process control methods for the manufacturing process of critical parts and work with the suppliers to ensure this is reflected in their process control plan

  • After a failure during production or OQC inspection at a supplier, run a rapid sprint analysis with design engineers to unblock the release of the shipment with risk-mitigative actions and keep production running with effective preventive measures

  • Update and implement quality control documentation to protect against future failures, based on root cause analysis that identified a component issue after, first flagged when a collar went offline on a farm in Australia

  • Audit the compliance with Halter’s quality requirements at a new supplier and work with the supplier to quickly close any non-conformances you found

What we are looking for:

  • 5+ years of experience in quality management for high-volume manufacturing. Production of electromechanical products is preferred

  • Committed to personal development and staying current with relevant industry standards, methods, and trends.

  • Proven experience in responding to and resolving quality issues rapidly to minimise production disruption

  • Demonstrated first principles thinking and ability to hone in on the most important issues during audit or reviewing problems

  • Experience in working with suppliers to achieve required outcomes based on context

  • High proficiency (written, verbal and reading) in English and Mandarin (preferred)

  • Relevant quality-related qualifications such as ASQ certification (for example CQE or CQA) are beneficial, as is formal Internal Auditor Certification

  • Willing to travel regularly around APAC (25%+ of your time)

  • Someone who will thrive in a close team environment and can work well in the self-directed and demanding environment of a rapidly scaling company
